name: Amazon SES
summary: Amazon SES is Amazon's low-cost email sending service that you connect directly through your own AWS account.

free_plan_covers.note: No ongoing free plan. New accounts get 3,000 emails a month free for the first 12 months only, then every email is billed.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Pricing is pay-as-you-go from about $0.10 per 1,000 emails, with no monthly plan or minimum on the standard tier.

portability.note: SES sends over standard SMTP as well as its API, so switching providers mainly means changing SMTP credentials.

sdk_typescript.note: The official @aws-sdk/client-sesv2 package, part of the AWS SDK for JavaScript v3, has TypeScript types built in.

setup.step: Create an AWS account, then verify at least one email address or domain to send from in the SES console.
Request production access to move out of the sandbox; until approved you can only send to your own verified addresses.
Install the SDK with npm install @aws-sdk/client-sesv2.
Create an IAM user scoped to SES sending and add its access key, secret key, and region to your environment file.
Send email from a server route using SESv2Client and SendEmailCommand.

builder_notes: New accounts start in the SES sandbox and can only send to verified addresses until you request production access, which can take up to 24 hours.
Keep AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY out of client code; call SES only from server-side routes using an IAM user scoped to ses:SendEmail.
